newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent ends down 24 cts on a wave of late selli.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent ends down 24 cts on a wave of late selli.

text.p: IPE Brent ended lower on Thursday after a bout of selling just ahead of the close undermined the market.

The June contract ended down 24 cents at $18.28 a barrel having been stable for most of the day. But in the last hour of trading prices climbed to the days high of $18.60 before falling quickly to a low of $18.26 a few minute ahead of the close.
"It was just technical selling at the end," said a broker.
Wet Brent crude looked a shade softer on Thursday after a U.S. refiner bought the last cargo it required to fill a VLCC due to load around May 10 for a transatlantic trip.
"It's looks like they're all done now and that could remove some support from Dated (Brent)," said a trader.
Other North Sea crudes were stable with holidays in most European countries keeping activity thin.
Refinery margins remain reasonably healthy in the West although well below highs seen last month.
In Europe a complex refinery makes about $2.15 a barrel running Brent compared to a high of $2.88 set about three weeks ago. "Margins aren't bad but the pressure is beginning to tell," said a trader.
Earlier, gas oil futures closed lower.
May gas oil closed 75 cents weaker at $171 a tonne. "It has been very quiet, there is really nothing happening," said one IPE broker.
Gas oil looked supported at $169.50 and then $166. "If it can hold at $169.50 it will have room to go higher, maybe to $175 and $177," said a trader.

Some brokers felt gas oil was waiting for a sell-off after several days of gains. Swaps brokers said the market may come under renewed downward pressure from Asia where May and June slipped 10 cents a barrel during the day.
